# SCI-MAP v0.1 PTC-Handoff Stage A Launch

Date: `2026-08-26`

Status: bounded Stage A reopening launched; formal MAP contract unchanged

## Purpose

The scientific owner approved reopening SCI-MAP v0.1 for one bounded reason:
the existing MAP packet predates the frozen PTC-to-MAP handoff and the current
producer/VAL ownership boundary. This is a recovery-and-reconciliation lane,
not a new derivation of ordinary mapmaking and not permission to revisit every
open MAP question.

The reopening follows the
[Scientific Contract Library Program](../../../README.md), the
[downstream roadmap](../../../DOWNSTREAM_CONTRACT_ROADMAP_2026-08-26.md), and
the approved
[ALIGN-to-MAP owner decisions](../../../ALIGN_TO_MAP_HORIZONTAL_OWNER_DECISIONS_2026-08-26.md).

## Reopening Trigger

The current MAP authority says that ordinary MAP input is calibrated SCI-CAL
data and attributes eligibility/precedence production to VAL. Those statements
are inconsistent with later governing authority:

- frozen PTC defines its transformed timestream as the authoritative
  PTC-to-MAP intermediate;
- ordinary map production has no inferred direct CAL-to-MAP fallback;
- PTC-produced availability is necessary but MAP owns the additional policy
  for its named map use; and
- VAL registers and evaluates owner-authored policy rather than becoming the
  policy author.

The owner has also supplied exact horizontal decisions for response and
uncertainty disclosure, versioned later derivatives, and ALIGN/AST versus MAP
coordinate/projection ownership.

## Admitted Stage A Authorities

Stage A may inspect and reconcile only:

- the current SCI-MAP v0.1 package and its existing owner-decision ledger;
- frozen SCI-PTC v0.1/r0.5, including its authoritative MAP handoff and
  disabled-routing rules;
- the current SCI-VAL source-binding register and evaluator/registry boundary;
- the frozen ALIGN, AST, RTC, and CAL interface facts needed to identify the
  PTC-to-MAP product; and
- the approved horizontal owner-decision record named above.

Implementation code, audit findings, repairs, tests, reductions, Unity
evidence, achieved performance, and production behavior remain outside the
implementation-blind author channel.

## Required Stage A Outputs

1. A prior-work delta record that identifies what the existing MAP derivation
   already answers and what the later authorities supersede.
2. A sanitized revised Scope Brief or bounded supersession cover that states
   the exact PTC-to-MAP input, MAP-owned admission, response/uncertainty
   disclosure, later-product versioning, and coordinate/projection ownership.
3. A content-bound author packet and source manifest containing no
   implementation, audit, repair, validation, or performance leakage.
4. An explicit mapping from every approved horizontal decision to existing or
   append-only normative identifiers and to any affected open owner decision.
5. Scientific-owner approval of the exact revised packet before Stage B.

## Locked Exclusions

This reopening does not authorize:

- editing frozen ALIGN, AST, RTC, CAL, or PTC contracts;
- deciding one-hot versus fractional projection, projection normalization,
  edge/boundary treatment, or additional projection classes;
- deciding the support-threshold numerical domain or unrelated MAP-local
  owner questions;
- importing JINC, NOI, filtering, source fitting, Pointing/OOF interpretation,
  Beammap inference, or FRUIT feedback;
- maximum-likelihood mapmaking;
- implementation changes, conformity claims, validation, Unity work,
  performance claims, package freeze, or production-readiness claims.

The existing 52 requirement IDs and 25 prediction IDs remain stable during
Stage A. A later revision may amend their wording in place where an authority
has superseded a premise and may append new IDs only for genuinely new
obligations.

## Gate And Current State

Stage A is launched. The prior-work delta, proposed bounded scope
supersession, sanitized authority extract, decision mapping, and content-bound
author-packet manifest are prepared for owner review. No Stage B author has
been dispatched. The owner must approve the exact sanitized packet first.
Because this program requires explicit owner approval before using Ultra
effort, that approval must also be obtained before the implementation-blind
Stage B authoring round begins.
